title: Chanthaburi & Trat 3-Day Road Trip Along Thailand's East Coast | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night Chanthaburi-to-Trat road trip: the Chanthaboon riverside community, the Cathedral, Phlio Waterfall, then the coastal road past Nern Nang Phaya into Trat, Laem Ngop, Ban Nam Chiao and Black Sand Beach — with timings, fees and a real budget.
keywords: Chanthaburi Trat trip, Chanthaburi Trat 3 day 2 night itinerary, Chanthaburi coastal road, Nern Nang Phaya, Phlio Waterfall, Laem Ngop, Ban Nam Chiao
h1:
Chanthaburi & Trat in 3 Days
Along the East Coast
intro: The far eastern provinces of Thailand have two neighbours that sit side by side, yet most people only pick one — even though you can easily drive straight from one to the other. Chanthaburi is known for its old riverside town, gemstones, fruit and waterfalls, while Trat is the last stretch of mainland with open sea and islands. This 3-day plan stitches the two together: start with the Chanthaboon riverside community in the morning, catch Phlio Waterfall on the way, then follow the coastal road past Nern Nang Phaya into Trat, and finish at Laem Ngop and Black Sand Beach. We've laid out the timing and the stops so you don't end up doubling back or driving past the good spots most people miss.

blocks.html: From Bangkok, Chanthaburi is about a 3-4 hour drive, and from Chanthaburi town it's only another hour or so to Trat town along Sukhumvit Road (Highway 3), a distance of roughly 70 km. The whole loop comes to around 330-400 km. A private car makes this trip far easier, because the heart of it is driving the coastal road that public transport simply can't reach. Day one covers Chanthaburi's old town, day two follows the coast into Trat, and day three picks up Laem Ngop, Black Sand Beach and some local gifts to take home before you head back.

blocks.title: Know the route before you set off
blocks.html: The prettiest stretch is Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road, the long coastal road of the east, passing Chao Lao Beach, Laem Sadet and the Nern Nang Phaya viewpoint before it loops back onto the main Sukhumvit Road to Trat. If you let GPS take an inland shortcut, it may push you onto the highway and you'll miss the sea views entirely. Set 'Nern Nang Phaya Viewpoint' as your destination first, then set the next leg to Trat.

items: Day 1 — Chanthaburi old town Chanthaboon riverside community, the Cathedral, the gem market, then overnight in Chanthaburi town

Day 2 — Phlio Waterfall + coastal drive into Trat Phlio Waterfall in the morning, the Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit coastal road past Nern Nang Phaya, seafood at Laem Sing, then cross into Trat and stay in town
Day 3 — Laem Ngop + Black Sand Beach Ban Nam Chiao, Laem Ngop, Black Sand Beach, pick up gifts, then drive home

blocks.html: On the first day, cover everything in Chanthaburi town first. All three stops are close enough to walk between, so there's no rush to drive off anywhere — save your energy for tomorrow's long coastal drive.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Chanthaboon Riverside, the Cathedral, the Gem Market

items.note: The Tha Luang quarter is an old street along the Chanthaburi River, more than 300 years old and about 900 metres long, lined with old wooden shophouses, the Luang Rajamaitri Historic Inn, the Rocket-brand ice cream shop, and local dishes like Chanthaburi crab noodles. Come early on a weekday while it's still quiet and you'll have an easy time taking photos.

items.activity: Cross Niramol Bridge to the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
items.note: The largest Catholic church in Thailand, over a hundred years old, sits directly across from the riverside community — you can simply walk over the bridge. Inside it's decorated with stained glass and a statue of the Virgin Mary adorned with Chanthaburi gems. Entry is free; dress modestly.

items.activity: Lunch: Chanthaburi crab noodles / mu chamuang
items.note: Chanthaburi crab noodles are the local specialty, while mu chamuang is a regional pork curry with a sour kick from chamuang leaves. You'll find both at restaurants in the old town — a good fill-up before you carry on to the market.

items.activity: Walk the Chanthaburi gem market (busiest Fri-Sun)
items.note: Si Chan Road and Trok Krachang are the centre of the gem trade, busiest at the weekend. You'll see real cutting and trading going on. On a weekday the market is quiet — you can still soak up the atmosphere, and even if you're not buying it's a pleasant stroll.

items.activity: Stop at a riverside cafe / rest
items.note: The old town has several cafes set in old buildings. Sit back, catch the river breeze in the afternoon, and save your energy for tomorrow's long drive.

items.activity: Dinner in town + one night in Chanthaburi
items.note: Staying in Chanthaburi town for the first night is the most convenient, with accommodation at every price level. Tomorrow you can check out and head for the coast mid-morning.

blocks.title: Time your day around the gem market
blocks.html: If you want to see the gem market truly busy, line up your first day with a Friday, Saturday or Sunday, since it's quiet on weekdays. The riverside community and the Cathedral are open every day, so you can visit those whenever.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Phlio Waterfall, the Coast, into Trat

blocks.html: Today is the highlight of the trip. Catch Phlio Waterfall in the morning, then follow the Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit coastal road past Nern Nang Phaya before turning onto Sukhumvit Road to cross into Trat in the afternoon. It's the day with the most driving, so leave room to stop for photos and seafood.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Phlio Waterfall → Nern Nang Phaya → Trat

items.activity: Check out, then head to Phlio Waterfall
items.note: Namtok Phlio National Park is about 14 km from Chanthaburi town. The waterfall runs clear year-round, with a school of soro brook carp in the pool. It's about a 500-metre walk from the car park. Entry is around 40 THB for adults, 20 THB for children, and it's open roughly 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

items.activity: Enjoy the falls + see Along Korn Stupa and the old pyramid
items.note: Within the waterfall grounds are the Along Korn Stupa and a pyramid built in the reign of King Rama V — a small piece of history many people don't know is there. You can take them in on the walk to the falls.

items.activity: Drive onto Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road (the coastal road)
items.note: Leaving Phlio, loop south onto the coastal road. The scenery shifts from fruit orchards to open sea — this is the prettiest stretch of driving on the whole trip. Take it slow; there are pull-offs for photos along the way.

items.activity: Stop at the Nern Nang Phaya viewpoint
items.note: This curving coastal road is the signature image of Chanthaburi, looking down on the road's bend and Khung Wiman Beach below. There's parking, a coffee shop, restrooms and a bike lane. Couples like to fasten love locks along the rail. It photographs best mid-morning when the sky is clear — the sun is strong, so bring a hat and water.

items.activity: Lunch: seaside seafood around Laem Sing
items.note: Laem Sing district is a fishing town at the mouth of the Chanthaburi River, with riverside seafood restaurants and fresh catch at better prices than the tourist spots. A good place to refuel before driving on to Trat.

items.activity: Drive into Trat via Sukhumvit Road
items.note: From Laem Sing, rejoin the main Sukhumvit Road and head for Trat, a distance of about 70-80 km. You'll pass fruit orchards and the provincial checkpoint on the way — keep your ID on you.

items.activity: Check in to your Trat hotel + walk the old town
items.note: Trat is small but has an old quarter along Thana Charoen Road, with wooden shophouses, coffee shops, and the Trat Museum in an old wooden building. It's a pleasant place to stroll and take photos in the early evening.
Trat is known for yen ta fo noodles and seafood, with an evening market full of cheap eats. Take a walk to settle dinner before bed. One night in Trat.

blocks.title: About the driving time on day two
blocks.html: Today is the most driving of the trip, and if you leave too late you may reach Trat after dark. We'd suggest leaving Chanthaburi before noon, which leaves room to stop for coastal photos and seafood and still get into Trat right around the cool of the evening.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Laem Ngop, Black Sand Beach, Gifts

blocks.html: On the last day, take in the charm of the Trat side before heading back: the Ban Nam Chiao community, Laem Ngop (the gateway to Koh Chang), and Black Sand Beach, which is hard to find anywhere else. Then pick up some gifts and drive home — Trat to Bangkok is about 315 km, roughly a 4.5-5 hour drive.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Ban Nam Chiao → Laem Ngop → Black Sand Beach → home

items.activity: Ban Nam Chiao community, Laem Ngop district
items.note: An old, Kinaree-award-winning community where Thai Buddhists and Muslims live side by side, with a mosque and a temple in the same quarter. Try the crisp tang me toffee and the famous khao kriap ya na crackers. Nearby is the 'Trust Bridge' (Wat Wong Bridge), an arching steel bridge whose reflection forms an oval like an eye — a popular photo spot.

items.activity: Laem Ngop viewpoint + Koh Chang Naval Battle Memorial
items.note: Laem Ngop is a fishing town and the gateway to Koh Chang, with the island appearing as a line of hills across the water. Nearby, the Koh Chang Naval Battle Memorial is worth a stop to learn the local history.

A beach of jet-black sand formed from natural minerals and shell sediment, about 2 km long. It's still off most people's radar — quiet and calm, good for a walk and photos. The sun gets strong by late morning, so bring a hat and water.

Laem Ngop is a source of shrimp paste, fish sauce and dried shrimp at source-level prices. Cap the trip with a big meal of blue crab, prawns and shellfish, then load up on gifts for the boot before you head back.
From Laem Ngop it's about 4.5-5 hours back to Bangkok. If you're not ready to head home, you could stay on at Koh Chang or stop at anything you missed in Chanthaburi on the way.

blocks.text: Tweak the Plan to Your Style

items.name: Only 2 days, 1 night
items.blurb: Combine Chanthaburi's old town with Phlio Waterfall on the first day, then follow the coast into Trat for Ban Nam Chiao and Black Sand Beach on day two. Just one night, in either Chanthaburi or Trat.

items.name: Add on Koh Chang
items.blurb: Trat is the gateway to Koh Chang. With 4-5 days, take the ferry from Laem Ngop to stay on Koh Chang, swim at Klong Plu Waterfall, or carry on to Koh Kood and Koh Mak where the water is clearer, then loop back.

items.name: For fruit lovers
items.blurb: If you come in April-June, work fruit orchards into the route. Both Chanthaburi and Trat are durian country — durian, mangosteen, rambutan — and there are several orchard fruit buffets along the way.

blocks.text: Rough Budget Per Person (3 Days, 2 Nights)

items: 2 nights' accommodation — 1 night in Chanthaburi + 1 in Trat, from around 1,200-2,000 THB per night for a mid-range place; split it between two of you
6-7 meals — around 900-1,500 THB, depending on how hard you go on the seafood
Phlio Waterfall entry — around 40 THB for adults, 20 THB for children
Fuel + tolls — the Bangkok-Chanthaburi-Trat-return route runs around 1,500-2,200 THB per car, split among everyone
Gifts — Chanthaburi gems, Laem Ngop shrimp paste, seasonal fruit, up to you
A mid-range total comes to around 2,500-4,000 THB per person (driving with 2-4 people makes it cheaper still)

blocks.text: Can You Do It Without a Car?

blocks.html: You can, but you'll miss the best part of the trip — the coastal road. Take a minivan or bus from Bangkok to Chanthaburi and get off in town, where the old town and gem market are within walking distance of each other. From there, catch a Chanthaburi-Trat minivan into Trat town, then use songthaews or motorbike taxis to reach Laem Ngop and Ban Nam Chiao. Phlio Waterfall and Nern Nang Phaya are off the regular bus routes, so you'd need to charter a vehicle or rent a motorbike. Without a car, this trip suits people who care more about the old towns and the food than the coastal sea views.

blocks.title: Best timing + driving safely
blocks.html: The best season for an easy, clear-skied coastal drive is November-February, when it's cool and the coastal road photographs beautifully. April-June is fruit season, when Chanthaburi's durian, mangosteen and rambutan are at their peak. The rainy season, May-October, brings frequent rain and the coastal road's tight curves get slippery — drive slowly, watch for cars pulled over for photos, and fill up before the coastal stretch since stations are far apart.

faq.q: Can you do Chanthaburi and Trat together in 3 days?
faq.a: Easily, if you have a car. Day one covers Chanthaburi's old town — the riverside community, the Cathedral and the gem market. Day two takes in Phlio Waterfall and the coastal road into Trat. Day three picks up Laem Ngop, Ban Nam Chiao and Black Sand Beach before you head home. If you also want to ferry across to Koh Chang or Koh Kood, allow 4-5 days.

faq.q: How long does it take to drive from Chanthaburi to Trat?
faq.a: Straight along Sukhumvit Road (Highway 3) it's about an hour, a distance of roughly 70 km. But if you choose to drive the Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit coastal road past Nern Nang Phaya and Laem Sing, it'll take longer — with stops for photos and seafood along the way — and it's well worth it for the views.

faq.q: Which days is the Chanthaburi gem market open?
faq.a: The gem market around Si Chan Road and Trok Krachang is busiest at the weekend, Friday through Sunday, when you can see real cutting and trading. On weekdays it's quiet — you can soak up the atmosphere but it's not lively. To see it in full swing, line up your first day with the weekend.

faq.q: Where is the Nern Nang Phaya coastal road, and is it hard to drive?
faq.a: It's on Chaloem Burapha Chonlathit Road, Chanthaburi's coastal route along the Chao Lao-Khung Wiman stretch, about 25 km from town. It's a curving coastal road with a viewpoint, coffee shops and parking. The road is paved and not hard to drive, but it gets slippery in the rainy season, so take care. Set your GPS to the Nern Nang Phaya viewpoint first, or a shortcut may push you onto the highway and you'll miss the sea views.

faq.q: What is Black Sand Beach in Trat, and can you actually visit?
faq.a: It's a beach of jet-black sand in Laem Ngop district, the colour coming from natural minerals and shell sediment, about 2 km long. It's still off most people's radar — quiet and calm, good for a walk and photos. Go in the morning before the sun gets strong. It's close to Laem Ngop and fits in right after Ban Nam Chiao.
